record.original_question: Can the analytical characterization problems for fractional integrals and derivatives be developed in the multidimensional setting for functions defined on R^n, rather than only for one-dimensional domains?

evidence.quote: Consider the problems formulated above in the multi-dimensional case, i.e., for the functions defined on R^n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop analytical characterizations of fractional integration and fractional differentiation operators for functions of several real variables. Concretely, for a suitable class of functions f : ℝⁿ → ℝ (or ℂ), one considers multidimensional analogues of the Riemann–Liouville/Riesz fractional integrals
  (I^α f)(x) = c(n,α) ∫_{ℝⁿ} |x − y|^{α−n} f(y) dy,  0 < Re α < n,
and the corresponding fractional derivatives D^α (e.g. Riesz, Marchaud, or hypersingular-integral-type derivatives).

Problem: Provide intrinsic analytical characterizations of the ranges and domains of these multidimensional operators. In particular:

(a) Characterize the image I^α(X) of a given function space X ⊂ L^p(ℝⁿ) (or X = L^p, Lipschitz, Hölder, Besov, Sobolev, etc.) by means of explicit conditions on the function itself (such as integrability, smoothness moduli, finite differences, hypersingular integrals, or behavior at infinity), without reference to the operator I^α.

(b) Determine necessary and sufficient analytical conditions on a function g : ℝⁿ → ℝ in order that g = I^α f for some f ∈ X, and analogously characterize when a function lies in the natural domain of D^α.

(c) Establish the multivariate analogues of one-dimensional inversion, composition, and mapping theorems for fractional integrals and derivatives in this characterization framework.

Resolve these characterization problems in the n-dimensional setting for n ≥ 2, paralleling the known one-dimensional theory.
artifact.status_search_result: Multidimensional fractional integration (Riesz potentials) and hypersingular-integral characterizations of their ranges on ℝⁿ have been extensively developed, notably in the monograph of Samko–Kilbas–Marichev and in Samko's "Hypersingular Integrals and Their Applications," which give characterizations of Riesz potentials of L^p functions for n ≥ 1 via finite differences and hypersingular integrals. However, complete intrinsic analytical characterizations for general function spaces and for general fractional-derivative-type operators in ℝⁿ remain an active research direction, with many cases still open.

status_evidence.title: Hypersingular Integrals and Their Applications (Samko)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the theory of hypersingular integrals to characterize ranges of Riesz potential operators of functions on R^n.
status_evidence.claim: Multidimensional characterizations of fractional integrals via hypersingular integrals have been developed.

status_evidence.title: Fractional Integrals and Derivatives: Theory and Applications (Samko, Kilbas, Marichev)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive treatment including multidimensional Riesz potentials and their characterizations.
status_evidence.claim: Significant portions of the multidimensional theory exist, though not all characterization questions are resolved.
